items.stem: Explain why compounding monthly gives a larger final value than compounding annually at the same nominal annual rate.
items.answer: Interest is added sooner, so each month's interest itself earns interest for the rest of the year; the effective annual rate (1 + r/1200)¹² − 1 exceeds r/100.

items.answer: (a) A 123 624.11, B 125 176.01 (b) B (c) 10 years (d) PV cancels

items.stem: Briefly explain why a depreciation model V = V₀(0.85)ⁿ never reaches zero, and whether this is realistic.

items.stem: Which term matches this description: "Paying off a loan through regular equal payments, each covering the interest due and part of the outstanding principal"?
items.answer: amortization
items.markingKey: D. This is the definition of amortization.

items.stem: The inflation rate is 3% per year. Which expression gives the value today of 1000 USD received in 4 years?
items.markingKey: 1000 ÷ 1.03⁴. Divide by the inflation factor for each year.

items.stem: For a delivery van costing 49200 CAD, offer A is 3.0% per annum over 5 years; offer B is 2.7% per annum over 8 years with a 800 CAD fee. Priya chooses B "because the interest rate is lower". Explain why this reasoning is incomplete.
items.answer: B costs 55 559.86 vs A 53 043.57 in total
items.markingKey: R1 the longer term and fee also affect cost; M1 totals A = 53 043.57, B = 55 559.86 (A1); R1 A is actually cheaper overall although B has lower monthly payments.

items.stem: A laptop bought for 2100 NZD depreciates at 19.8% per year. Explain why the value after n years is given by 2100(0.802)ⁿ and interpret the number 0.802.
items.answer: Each year the value is multiplied by 0.802
items.markingKey: R1 losing 19.8% leaves 80.2% of the previous value each year; R1 repeated multiplication by 0.802 gives the power n; 0.802 is the proportion of value kept each year (A1).

items.stem: Felix borrows 244000 GBP at 8.2% per annum, repaid by monthly payments of 2 360.05 GBP. Calculate the interest included in the first and second payments and explain why they differ.
items.markingKey: First: 244000 × 8.2/1200 = 1 667.33 (A1); balance 243 307.28 (M1); second: 1 662.60 (A1); R1 the balance has fallen, so less interest is charged.

items.stem: Sofia's salary of 35000 SGD rises by 3.0% while inflation over the same year is 4.9%. Explain, with a calculation, what happens to the real value of Sofia's salary.
items.answer: Falls: real value ≈ 34 366.06 SGD in last year's money
items.markingKey: New salary 36 050.00 (A1); in last year's prices 36 050.00 ÷ 1.049 = 34 366.06 (M1 A1); R1 this is less than 35000, so purchasing power falls.

items.stem: 29100 EUR is invested for 20 years at a nominal rate of 5.2% per annum. Compare the final values when interest is compounded annually and monthly, and explain the difference.

A small business borrows 9200 NZD at 6.1% per annum, to be repaid in 2 equal annual instalments. (a) Show that each instalment is 5 025.05 NZD, to 2 d.p. (b) Construct the amortization table for the first 2 years. (c) Explain how the table shows that interest is charged on the outstanding balance.
items.answer: (a) 5 025.05 (b) year 1: interest 561.20, principal 4 463.85, end balance 4 736.15; year 2: interest 288.90, principal 4 736.15, end balance 0.00 (c) interest falls as the balance falls

Hana wants to buy a family motorhome costing 61700 CAD. Option 1: a loan at 3.7% per annum compounded monthly over 5 years. Option 2: save 400 CAD at the end of each month in an account paying 3.2% per annum compounded monthly, and buy when the savings reach the price. (a) Find the total cost of option 1. (b) Find how many months option 2 takes. (c) Find the amount actually paid in by Hana under option 2. (d) Discuss one advantage of each option, assuming the price stays the same.
items.answer: (a) 67 677.92 (b) 130 months (c) 52 000.00 (d) loan gives immediate use; saving is cheaper
items.markingKey: (a) PMT = 1 127.97 (M1 A1), total 67 677.92 (A1). (b) TVM PV = 0, PMT = −400, FV = 61700, I% = 3.2 (M1): N = 129.37 → 130 months (A1). (c) 400 × 130 = 52 000.00 (A1). (d) R1 loan: immediate use of a family motorhome; R1 saving: costs less because interest is earned not paid (but price may rise with inflation).

items.stem: Outline the meaning of the term "annuity".
items.answer: A series of equal payments made at regular intervals, e.g. a pension paying a fixed amount each month

items.stem: In the IB approach to a TVM solver with inflation, what is entered for I%?
options: the interest rate plus the inflation rate
the interest rate minus the inflation rate
the interest rate times the inflation rate
items.answer: the interest rate minus the inflation rate
items.markingKey: B. I% = r − i gives the approximate real growth.

items.answer: (a) A 42 412.17, B 41 820.55 (b) A (c) 30 years (d) PV cancels
